hindi: अथवा उससे मिला हुआ अन्न कुत्ते या कौए को दे।
english: Or he should give food mixed with that to a dog or a crow.
notes: 'That' (tat) is presumably the blood under test in the preceding units; the line does not say so.

words.gram: past part. a-√bhuj, n. loc. sg.

hindi: उसके खाए जाने पर जीव यानी जीवरक्त, और न खाए जाने पर पित्त।
english: When that is eaten, jīva (life-blood); when it is not eaten, pitta.
notes: Elliptical: the verb (something like 'one should know it as') is carried from earlier units and not supplied. jīva is read as jīvarakta ('life-blood') of the preceding units; pitta here is the humour-related blood (cf. raktapitta) as the text uses it, no more is stated.

words.gloss: afflicted by thirst, fainting and intoxication

hindi: और मरण तक भी, प्यास, मूर्च्छा और मद से पीड़ित उसके लिए पित्त को नष्ट करने वाली क्रिया करे, और अतियोग में कहे हुए को भी करे।
english: And up to death, for him afflicted by thirst, fainting and intoxication (mada), he should carry out the pitta-destroying treatment and what is stated for excess (atiyoga).
notes: āmaraṇāt is literally 'up to death'; whether it means 'as long as danger of death lasts' is not stated. atiyogokta is read as 'what is stated for atiyoga (excess)'; the noun is unstated. Printed 'ārtta' normalised to ārta; 'tṛṇ-' is tṛṭ (thirst) before m.

words.gloss: blood of khaḍga (probably the rhinoceros) and the rest
by the method stated for excessive flow (atisruta)

hindi: और खड्ग यानी सम्भवतः गैंडे आदि का रक्त, अतिस्राव में कही गई विधि से, मधु सहित, शीघ्र ग्रहण करे।
english: And he should quickly take the blood of khaḍga (probably the rhinoceros) and the rest, with honey, by the method stated for excessive flow (atisruta).

text_flags.why: the 'r' after 'sruta' is unexplained; atisruta + ukta is expected; possible (alternatively atisrute rakte-ukta, 'stated for excessive flow of blood')

notes: khaḍga = rhinoceros (probable; khaḍga also means 'sword'); 'blood of khaḍga and the rest' is as printed, the others are not named. What 'excessive flow' (atisruta) refers to is not stated here; the method is stated elsewhere (not in this unit). Read on the corrected form; the printed form is doubtful.

words.gloss: with śyāmā (a plant; identity disputed), kāśmarya (Gmelina arborea, gmelina tree; standard), dūrvā (Cynodon dactylon, Bermuda grass; standard) and uśīra (Vetiveria zizanioides, vetiver root; standard)

hindi: अथवा श्यामा, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी, दूर्वा यानी दूब और उशीर यानी खस के साथ पकाया हुआ दूध, एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार बकरी के घृतमण्ड से युक्त, ठण्डा, बस्ति में डाले।
english: Or milk boiled with śyāmā (a plant of disputed identity), kāśmarya (gmelina tree), dūrvā (Bermuda grass) and uśīra (vetiver root), on a conjectural reading joined with goat's ghee-maṇḍa, cool, he should pour into the basti (enema).

text_flags.why: words run together and the middle 'ājamayuktam' is unclear (extra a before yukta?); conjectural, possible

notes: The token 'ghṛtamaṃḍājamayuktaṃśītaṃ' is run together and doubtful; the printed middle part is kept unsplit (unclear) and the translation reads it, conjecturally, as 'joined with goat's (ājam) ghee-maṇḍa' (ghṛtamaṇḍa = literal 'ghee-maṇḍa', see glossary). śyāmākāśmarya is read as śyāmā + kāśmarya (śyāmā disputed: Operculina turpethum and Ichnocarpus frutescens are among proposals); kāśmarya, dūrvā, uśīra are standard identifications. niṣecayet is literally 'should pour/instil'.

words.gloss: in the complications of properly administered emesis and purgation

hindi: और भली-भाँति प्रयुक्त वमन और विरेचन के शेष उपद्रवों में भी, रोग के अनुसार दोषों का विचार करके प्रतिकार करे, और बस्तिव्यापत्सिद्धि को देखे।
english: And in the remaining complications (upadrava) too, of emesis and purgation properly administered, he should counter them according to the disease, having regard to the doṣas, and should look to the basti-vyāpat-siddhi.

text_flags.why: long ā where ca is expected; possible

notes: 'cā samyak' is read as ca + samyak ('properly administered'); the alternative ca + a-samyak ('improperly administered') would suit a chapter on faulty administration but is not what is printed. basti-vyāpat-siddhi presumably names the chapter of that name (cf. the colophon style); literally 'cure of the complications of basti'. Printed 'vasti' normalised to basti.

hindi: इसी प्रकार दोनों भागों वाले शोधन में भी अवस्था के अनुसार उठ खड़ा हो।
english: Thus too, in cleansing through both portions (ubhayatobhāga), he should rise up according to the condition.
notes: ubhayatobhāga is probably cleansing by both the upper and lower ways (probable; the line does not say). uttiṣṭhet is literally 'should stand up'; the intended sense ('set to work, proceed') is not stated.

hindi: विरेचन में जो परिकर्तिका यानी काटने की पीड़ा है, वही वमन में कण्ठ की क्षति है; जो परिस्रव है, वह कफ का प्रसेक यानी बहना है; जो प्रवाहण है, वह शुष्क उद्गार यानी सूखी डकार है।
english: What is parikartikā (cutting pain) in purgation, that in emesis is injury of the throat (kaṇṭha-kṣaṇana); what is the discharge (parisrava), that is the flow of Kapha (kapha-praseka); what is straining (pravāhaṇa), that is dry belching (śuṣka-udgāra).

text_flags.why: missing space; hiatus, no sandhi, before iti (spacing only)

notes: Three equivalences between purgation and emesis; no verb is needed. kṣaṇana is literally 'hurting/wounding'; pravāhaṇa 'forcing down, straining' (cf. pravāhikā). Closing iti goes to notes only. Printed 'parikarttikā' normalised to parikartikā.

hindi: और इस विषय में ये हैं।
english: And on this point there are (the following).
notes: Lead-in formula introducing what follows; the thing that 'there are' (verses) is unstated, hence '(the following)'.

words.gram: past part. caus. a-√bhū, n. nom. sg.

hindi: अत्यधिक, अकाल में, थोड़ा, समान वीर्य यानी सामर्थ्य वालों से न भिगोया हुआ,
english: Excessive, at the wrong time, scanty, not soaked (bhāvita) with (ones) of equal potency (vīrya),
notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues in the next unit, where the subject (the medicine) appears. bhāvita 'soaked' is the glossary rendering (steeped, impregnated); akāle may be 'out of season' as well as 'at the wrong time'.

hindi: भली-भाँति संस्कार न किया हुआ, पुराना, औषध निश्चय ही बिगड़ जाएगा।
english: Improperly prepared, old, the medicine would surely go wrong (fail).
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in the previous unit (excess, wrong time, scanty, not soaked, improperly prepared, old: the medicine fails). jīrṇa 'old' follows the glossary; 'worn out, decayed' is possible.

hindi: वमन नहीं, बल्कि एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार बुरा वमन; बुरा विरेचन, रेचन नहीं।
english: Not vomiting (chardana) but, on a conjectural reading, bad vomiting; bad purging (durvireca), not purging (recana).

text_flags.why: damaged print: the vowel sign after 'rd' is missing; duś-chardaṃ ('bad vomiting') expected; possible

notes: The printed word 'duśchardṃ' is damaged and kept unsplit; the translation reads it conjecturally as 'bad vomiting'. The line seems to say that a failed emetic becomes bad vomiting and a failed purgative bad purging, but this is a conjecture. chardana / recana could also mean 'emetic' / 'purgative' (the substance).

hindi: औषध फिर पिलाए; वह उसे नष्ट करता है, क्योंकि वे वैसे ही हैं।
english: He should make (him) drink the medicine again; it destroys that (or him); for indeed they are so.
notes: The syntax is unclear: taṃ may be 'him' (the patient) or 'that' (the remaining doṣa); the subject of nihanti and the referent of te ('they') are not given in this unit. Rendered as literally as possible; the sense is uncertain.

hindi: जिसके पीया हुआ अनुलोमिक यानी स्वाभाविक दिशा में चलने वाला कफ से मिला हुआ ऊपर की ओर जाता है,
english: In whom what is drunk, ānulomika (going in the natural direction), goes upward mixed with Kapha,
notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues in the next unit. 'What is drunk' (pītam) is the medicine, unstated. ānulomika is literally 'going with the grain'; for a purgative this is probably downward (probable), but the line does not say.

words.gram: past part. caus. √laṅgh, m. acc. sg.

hindi: केवलों से वमन कराए गए, शुद्ध हुए और लंघन कराए गए उसे तो पिलाए।
english: But him who has been made to vomit with plain (ones), is cleansed and has been made to fast, he should make drink (it).
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of the previous unit. kevalaiḥ 'by plain/alone (ones)': what is plain (e.g. unmixed emetics) is not stated. The object of pāyayet (the medicine) is unstated.

words.gram: past part. vi-√bandh, m. loc. sg.

hindi: दोष के रुके रहने, थोड़ा होने और देर से बहने पर गरम जल पिए।
english: When the doṣa is held back, scanty, and flowing (only) after a long time, he should drink hot water.
notes: sravati is read as a locative participle agreeing with doṣe; it may also be 'it flows' (3 sg.). cirāt may be 'after a long time' or 'slowly'. The drinker (the patient) is unstated.

hindi: उससे आध्मान यानी अफारा, वमन, तृष्णा और विबन्ध यानी रुकावट शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: By that, distension (ādhmāna), vomiting, thirst and obstruction (vibandha) subside.
notes: ādhmāna = abdominal distension, bloating (standard). The singular verb serves the whole list. 'That' (tena) is the hot water of the previous unit.

hindi: यदि दोष से रुकी हुई औषध न ऊपर जाती है और न नीचे,
english: If the medicine, obstructed by a doṣa, proceeds neither upward nor downward,
notes: GROUPING: the 'if' clause; the main clause is in the next unit. Printed 'pravarttate' normalised to pravartate.

hindi: डकार या अंगों में शूल सहित होने पर वहाँ स्वेद का प्रयोग करे।
english: In that case, (if it is) with belching or with pain in the limbs, he should apply sweating (sveda).
notes: GROUPING: completes the 'if' clause of the previous unit. The two adjectives are accusative neuter and presumably agree with an unstated noun (the medicine or the condition); '(if it is)' is supplied only for readability. avacārayet: glossary 'should apply' (OPEN).

words.gloss: (a person) properly purged, with belching; the medicine

hindi: भली-भाँति विरेचित और डकार वाले की औषध को शीघ्र खुरचकर ऊपर निकाले।
english: Of (a person) properly purged and with belching, the medicine he should quickly scrape up.
notes: The compound samyag-virikta-sodgāra-bheṣaja is read as 'properly purged, with belching, the medicine' with bheṣaja the object of ullikhet; this construction is uncertain. ullikhet is literally 'should scrape out/up'; the method is not stated.

words.gloss: when it does not set in motion

hindi: न पचे हुए और प्रवृत्त न होने पर वैद्य बहुत ठण्डों से रोके।
english: But when (it is) undigested and does not set in motion, the physician should check (it) with very cold (ones).
notes: The subject (the medicine) and what is checked are unstated. stambhayet is literally 'should make rigid, stop'. ajīrṇa taken as 'undigested'.

hindi: कभी-कभी कफ से रुकी हुई औषध छाती में ठहरी रहती है।
english: Sometimes the medicine, obstructed by Kapha (śleṣman), stays in the chest.
notes: Printed 'kadācicchleṣmaṇā' is kadācit + śleṣmaṇā.

hindi: कफ के क्षीण होने पर, सायंकाल या रात्रि में, वह प्रवृत्त होता है।
english: When Kapha has diminished, in the evening or at night, it moves on.

text_flags.why: letters transposed; sāyāhna is the standard form; possible

notes: 'It' is the medicine of the previous unit (unstated). Printed 'pravarttate' normalised to pravartate.

hindi: जीर्ण यानी पचे हुए होने पर, ठहरे रहने पर, अथवा ऊपर गए हुए होने पर भी, रूक्ष अन्न खिलाए।
english: When (it is) digested, staying, or even gone upward, he should feed dry food.

text_flags.why: the accusative -m of rūkṣānnam appears lost (or rūkṣānnān); possible

notes: The syntax is uncertain: jīrṇe, tiṣṭhati and ūrdhvagate are read as three locatives (absolute) of an unstated subject (the medicine / Kapha). jīrṇa is rendered 'digested' here, not 'old' (the glossary rendering, used in an earlier unit for aged medicine), because the context is digestion; 'old' remains possible. tiṣṭhati may also be a verb ('it stays').

hindi: किन्तु औषध के वायु से रुकने पर किसी दूसरे को स्नेह और लवण सहित पिए।
english: But when the medicine (is held) by Vāyu (wind), he should drink another (one), with fat (sneha) and salt.

text_flags.why: sa-sneha expected; one 'sa' appears lost; possible

notes: Elliptical: the participle (probably ruddha, 'held', carried from the earlier unit about Kapha) is not in the line. 'Another (one)' is a drink or medicine, unstated. sasnehalavaṇa could also mean 'salt with fat' (bahuvrīhi) instead of 'fat and salt'.

words.gloss: thirst, delusion, giddiness, fainting and the rest

hindi: प्यास, मोह, भ्रम, मूर्च्छा आदि हो सकते हैं, और औषध के पचते समय।
english: Thirst, delusion, giddiness, fainting and the rest may occur, and while the medicine is being digested.

text_flags.why: tṛṇa ('grass') is not apt; tṛṇ- (tṛṭ, 'thirst') as in the earlier 'tṛṇmūrcchā' is expected; possible

notes: The last clause is as printed: 'and while the medicine is being digested' qualifies the occurrence of the listed signs. jīryati may be read 'is digested / ages' (see glossary jīrṇa).

hindi: वहाँ पित्त को नष्ट करने वाली, मीठी और ठण्डी औषध प्रशस्त है।
english: In that case a medicine that is pitta-destroying, sweet and cool is recommended.
notes: svādu 'sweet' may also be 'pleasant-tasting'.

words.gloss: from salivation, nausea, obstruction and horripilation (hair standing on end)

hindi: लालास्राव, हृल्लास यानी मिचली, विष्टम्भ और रोमहर्ष यानी रोंगटे खड़े होने के कारण कफ से ढके होने पर,
english: From salivation, nausea (hṛllāsa), obstruction (viṣṭambha) and horripilation (hair standing on end), when (it is) enveloped by Kapha,

text_flags.why: hallāsa is not a word; hṛllāsa ('nausea') expected; possible

notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues in the next unit ('in that case ... the medicine'). The ablative is read as marking the signs from which the Kapha covering is known; the subject (the medicine) is unstated. hṛllāsa = nausea (standard); viṣṭambha = obstruction, stiffness, binding (here as printed).

hindi: वहाँ तीक्ष्ण और उष्ण, कटु आदि, कफ को हटाने वाली, हितकर औषध।
english: In that case, the medicine that is sharp and hot, pungent and the rest, Kapha-dispelling, beneficial.

text_flags.why: kad- is not a stem; kaṭu-ādi expected; possible

notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in the previous unit. Nominal sentence, no verb supplied. kaṭvādi could also name a drug group beginning with kaṭu (unclear).

hindi: गुदा की विपरीत गति, ग्रथितत्व यानी गाँठदार होना, भारीपन सहित।
english: Contrary movement of the anus, knottedness (grathitatva), with heaviness.
notes: A list of signs or complications; no verb. pāyoḥ is taken with gatiḥ; what is 'knotted' is not stated.

hindi: दोष का उत्क्लेश, अत्यधिक आध्मान, परिकर्त यानी काटने की पीड़ा, परिस्रव यानी बहना।
english: Stirring up of the doṣa (utkleśa), severe distension (ādhmāna), cutting pain (parikarta), discharge (parisrava).
notes: Continues the list of the previous unit. Printed 'parikarttaḥ' normalised to parikartaḥ.

words.gloss: pravāhikā (straining with frequent loose stools; roughly dysentery; probable)

hindi: प्रवाहिका यानी सम्भवतः पेचिश, हृदय का ग्रहण, और सारे अंगों का जकड़ जाना।
english: Pravāhikā (probably dysentery), seizing of the heart (hṛdgrahaṇa), gripping of the whole body.
notes: pravāhikā = dysentery with straining (probable). hṛd can be 'heart' or 'chest'. Continues the list.

words.gloss: with the flow of all the dhātus

hindi: सर्वधातुस्रव के साथ ये बारह उपचारों सहित कही गई हैं।
english: With the flow of all the dhātus, these twelve are stated, with their remedies.
notes: The instrumental is read 'together with' (the flow of all dhātus counted in the twelve); the text does not itself list the twelve here. The word 'etā' is etāḥ with the visarga lost before d.

words.gloss: from a lapse in the application (yoga)

hindi: योग यानी प्रयोग के भ्रंश से व्यापदें, विविध विरेचन में भी,
english: Complications (vyāpad) from a lapse in the application (yoga), even in purgation of various kinds,
notes: GROUPING: this and the next two units form one sentence (continued in 109 and 110); no verb here. yoga may also mean 'combination (of the drug)'; vibhraṃśa 'slip, failure'.

words.gram: pres. part. pass. ud-√pad, f. loc. pl.

hindi: और संशोधन के विभ्रम से उत्पन्न होती हुई उन-उन व्यापदों में,
english: And in those various complications that are arising through a deviation in cleansing (saṃśodhana),
notes: GROUPING: part of the sentence that is completed in the next unit. tāsu tāsu 'in those and those', i.e. in each of those.

hindi: इसी निर्देश से शीघ्र सिद्धि के लिए प्रयत्न करे; क्योंकि शास्त्र नय और दुर्नय का प्रकाश है।
english: By this very direction he should quickly strive for the cure (siddhi); for the śāstra is the light of sound and unsound conduct (naya, durnaya).
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of the two previous units. Printed "'nayaivāśu" is anayā eva āśu (the avagraha stands for the initial a). naya 'right policy/method', durnaya 'wrong policy'; siddhi 'accomplishment, cure'.

words.gloss: Vamana-virecana-vyāpat-siddhi (cure of the complications of emesis and purgation)

hindi: इस प्रकार वमन-विरेचन-व्यापत्सिद्धि नामक तृतीय अध्याय।
english: Thus the third chapter, named Vamana-virecana-vyāpat-siddhi (the cure of the complications of emesis and purgation).
notes: Colophon. The opening || is a printed mark. The title is read as vamana-virecana-vyāpat-siddhi 'cure (siddhi) of the complications (vyāpad) of emesis and purgation'. Closing iti belongs to the colophon formula.
